reasons.reason: Conditioning on Y = y, the chance that X exceeds 2y is exp(-2 lambda y). Averaging that over the exponential density of Y with rate mu gives mu divided by mu plus twice lambda.
Doubling Y doubles its rate to 2 mu, and for two competing exponentials the chance that the lambda one ends up larger is lambda over the sum of the rates, so lambda over lambda plus 2 mu.
The six factors (x - omega^k) multiply out to 1 + x + x^2 + ... + x^6, the cyclotomic polynomial. Setting x = 1 gives seven ones added together, which is 7.
Because omega^7 equals 1, the polynomial 1 - x^7 vanishes at omega, and the product of the factors 1 - omega^k is that polynomial evaluated at a root, so the whole product collapses to zero.

Applying T over and over pushes each vector out of the image and into the kernel, and since kernel and image split V cleanly, repeated application eventually kills everything, which is exactly nilpotence.

An invertible map satisfies this with a zero kernel and the zero map satisfies it with a zero image, and doubling every vector satisfies it too, so the condition forces none of those listed properties.
Counting twos in 12! gives 6 + 3 + 1 = 10 exactly, while 11! and 10! only reach 8, so 12 is the first factorial that 2^10 divides.
2^10 is 1024, and 10! is 3628800, which is thousands of times larger and full of even factors like 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, so 10! already absorbs 1024 and nothing smaller does.
For 3x + 5y = 100 the value of y must be 2 more than a multiple of 3, so y = 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, each giving positive x from 30 down to 5.
Here x has to be a multiple of 5 for 100 - 3x to be divisible by 5, and stepping x from 5 up to 25 in fives gives five values, each leaving a positive whole y.

Diagonalizing over R needs a full basis of real eigenvectors, which happens precisely when every root of the characteristic polynomial is real and each eigenspace is as large as that root's multiplicity.
The spectral theorem says a real symmetric matrix always has an orthonormal basis of real eigenvectors, so symmetry is the property that makes a real matrix diagonalizable over the reals.
Separating gives dy/y = dx/(x ln x), and since the derivative of ln x is 1/x, the right side integrates to ln x, so ln y = ln x plus a constant and y is proportional to x.
Separating variables gives dy/y = dx/(x ln x). Substituting u = ln x turns the right side into du/u, so ln y = ln(ln x) plus a constant, and y is a multiple of ln x.
X greater than k means the first success arrives after trial k, and with each trial succeeding at rate p, that tail works out to one minus (1-p) raised to the k.
X exceeding k just means the first k trials all failed, and since each trial fails independently with probability 1-p, that probability is (1-p) multiplied by itself k times.
Every 3 by 3 matrix splits into a symmetric part plus a skew-symmetric part, so the skew-symmetric matrices still reach all nine entry positions, and the subspace has dimension nine.
A skew-symmetric 3 by 3 matrix has zeros on the diagonal, and each entry below the diagonal is the negative of one above, so only the three entries above the diagonal are free.
Subtracting mu and dividing by sigma turns any normal variable into a standard normal with mean 0 and variance 1, whose density is 1 over sqrt(2 pi) times exp(-y^2/2).
Standardizing only shifts the center and rescales the axis, so the bell shape exp(-y^2 / (2 sigma^2)) carries over with the mean removed and the spread still sitting in the exponent.
A symmetric matrix is pinned down by its diagonal together with one mirrored row of off-diagonal values, so counting n diagonal entries and n mirrored entries gives 2n free parameters.
The free entries of a symmetric matrix are the ones on or above the diagonal: n on the diagonal plus n(n-1)/2 above it, which adds up to n(n+1)/2.
The smallest possible total distance to a set of points equals the combined spread between them, and adding the gaps from 1 to 3, 3 to 5 and 1 to 5 gives 2 + 2 + 4 = 8.
A sum of absolute distances is smallest at the median point, here x = 3, where the three terms are 2, 0 and 2, giving a total of 4.
The characteristic polynomial is lambda squared minus the trace times lambda, which here is lambda^2 - 5 lambda = lambda(lambda - 5), so the eigenvalues come out as 0 and 5.
The eigenvalues must add to the trace and multiply to the determinant, so they are the roots of lambda^2 - 5 lambda + 6, which factors as (lambda - 2)(lambda - 3).
Squaring the difference, the two cross pieces carrying +8 sqrt(2) and -8 sqrt(2) cancel each other, leaving 18 + 18 = 36, and the square root of 36 is 6.
Since (4 + sqrt(2))^2 = 18 + 8 sqrt(2) and (4 - sqrt(2))^2 = 18 - 8 sqrt(2), the two roots are 4 + sqrt(2) and 4 - sqrt(2), whose difference is 2 sqrt(2).
The vertex of the parabola sits at x = -k/2 with height 1 - k^2/4, and that height clears zero once k^2 reaches 4, which means k at least 2 or at most -2.
An upward parabola stays strictly above the axis only when it has no real roots, so the discriminant k^2 - 4 must be negative, which puts k strictly between -2 and 2.
